Description: A function or method in ANOTHER file that makes most of the same distinctive qualified calls as a function in the scoped file: one mechanism written twice, usually kept in sync by nothing but a comment, so the next change to either copy has to be made in both. Structural clone detection misses these because the copies are rewritten rather than pasted. One finding per partner function, located at the partner; metric = shared distinctive calls x 100 / the smaller of the two call sets. A call is distinctive when at most 15 functions in the db make it, so ubiquitous calls (fmt.Errorf, errors.Is) never count; a pair needs at least 3 shared distinctive calls. Run it scoped to a changed file (--source-id); unscoped it reports every overlapping pair from both sides, which on a codebase with versioned API adapters is mostly intended copies. Known false positives: thin wrappers that legitimately share one client's call surface, and parallel adapters for two versions of the same API.
Query: WITH fns AS (SELECT DISTINCT node_id FROM v_defs WHERE canonical_kind IN ('function', 'method')), calls AS (SELECT DISTINCT r.referrer_node_id AS fn, r.source_id, r.token FROM v_refs r JOIN fns ON fns.node_id = r.referrer_node_id WHERE r.token LIKE '%%.%%' AND r.source_id NOT LIKE '%%_test.go'), df AS (SELECT token, COUNT(DISTINCT fn) AS d FROM calls GROUP BY token), rare AS (SELECT c.fn, c.source_id, c.token FROM calls c JOIN df ON df.token = c.token WHERE df.d <= 15), sz AS (SELECT fn, COUNT(*) AS n FROM rare GROUP BY fn), pairs AS (SELECT a.fn AS fa, b.fn AS fb, b.source_id AS sb, COUNT(*) AS shared FROM rare a JOIN rare b ON a.token = b.token AND a.source_id <> b.source_id WHERE 1 = 1 %s GROUP BY a.fn, b.fn, b.source_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3) SELECT p.sb AS source_id, p.fb AS node_id, COALESCE(x.start_byte, 0), COALESCE(x.end_byte, 0), COALESCE(x.start_row, 0), COALESCE(x.start_col, 0), (p.shared * 100 / MIN(sa.n, sb.n)) AS metric FROM pairs p JOIN sz sa ON sa.fn = p.fa JOIN sz sb ON sb.fn = p.fb LEFT JOIN v_ast x ON x.node_id = p.fb ORDER BY metric DESC, p.shared DESC, p.sb
